answer: A riverside network keeps its garden registry honest by tying each identity to a distinct live data source it alone tends. The first newcomer stewards 1 source, the tenth 10, and the twentieth 20, each unique, never shared between names. A farmer of fakes faces a bill that climbs with every identity: 20 fakes demand 210 distinct sources, and one opal-bright feed cannot cover twenty strangers, each needing its own operator and provenance. Like wells along a river, each name needs its own spring; bulk farming fails because sources cannot be cloned or bought in bulk.
